text:
alex: Heads up — Customer-Delta reported a regression after the 1.3 rollout: streaming sessions occasionally drop out around prefix cache warmup. They flagged it as blocking their acceptance tests.

maria: Thanks Alex. Do we have an incidence rate? Is this reproducible in staging or limited to their workload? :thinking_face:

devin: Quick numbers from their logs: ~7% of long-running streams see a 1-2s stall then resume. Reproducible with their prompt patterns (long context + intermittent user edits). Staging with the same seed shows ~2%.

sophie: That feels like a quality regression vs feature gap. Impacted customers are on Dedicated but their SLA is sensitive. Suggest we triage as P1 and aim for a hotfix canary.

jamal: Can we soften the heuristic that changes KV eviction during warmup? Patch idea: fallback to legacy eviction for sessions > 8k tokens. Small diff, low risk.

alex: Patch sounds reasonable. What's the rollout plan? We should avoid broad rollback unless necessary.

devin: Proposal: deploy patch to a single Dedicated cluster (canary) with metric watch: stream success rate, p50/p95 latency, CPU/GPU utilization. 48h hold then expand if no regressions.

maria: Also add a customer-facing mitigation: enable prefix-caching=false toggle for Customer-Delta while we validate. That buys time while patch goes through canary.

sophie: QA checklist for canary: run Customer-Delta acceptance suite, stress test 200 concurrent streams, smoke for memory leaks. pm-bot will create a checklist item.

pm-bot: Created task INF-4821: hotfix-canary-eviction-fallback with assignees @devin @jamal @sophie. Link: https://redwood/tasks/INF-4821 :white_check_mark:

jamal: If canary shows improvement, we should coordinate a quick gradual rollout across Dedicated clusters and then a hosted API deploy with feature flag defaulting to on for affected model families.

alex: One product note — let's capture acceptance criteria for closing this: (1) Customer-Delta acceptance suite passes for 48h on canary; (2) stream stall rate <= 0.5% at 95th percentile; (3) no memory/regression alerts in Prometheus.

maria: Agree. Also log the cost delta so we can decide if this stays permanent or we rework the heuristic as an enhancement next quarter.

devin: I'll open the PR with the fallback and start canary today. ETA for PR review: 3 hours. Will post updates here.

sophie: Thanks. I'll prep QA and the rollout playbook. If anything changes we escalate to oncall.

alex: Sounds good. Tag me when canary metrics are up.

maria: Thanks team — prioritize customer acceptance over pushing the heuristic. We'll treat the long-term fix as a Q2 enhancement once stabilized. :thumbsup:
